# SUBDURAL EMPYEMA

Most cases (60-90%) result from extension of sinusitis or otitis media (contiguous sources). Surgical drainage is necessary. Obtain material for culture. For patients with severe penicillin allergy consult Infectious Diseases.

# Consult Neurosurgery, Neurology, and Infectious Disease

# Duration of Therapy

Treat for 4-6 weeks

---

References:

- Mandell chapter: Subdural Empyema, Epidural Abscess, and Suppurative Intracranial Thrombophlebitis
- Sanford keyword: Subdural empyema
Therapy:
## Empiric Treatment for Infection from Contiguous Source

Preferred:

Ceftriaxone 2 gm IV q12h ($) [M] <AND> metronidazole 15 mg/kg IV q12h ($) [DI]

Alternative:

Assessment of beta-lactam reaction

Meropenem 2 gm IV q8h ($$) R,O

## Empiric Treatment for Unknown Source, History of MRSA Infection or Colonization

Ceftriaxone 2 gm q12h ($) [M] <AND> metronidazole 15 mg/kg IV q12h ($) [DI]
<AND> vancomycin 15mg/kg IV q12h ($) [R]

Alternative:

Assessment of beta-lactam reaction

Meropenem 2 gm IV q8h ($$) R,O  <AND> vancomycin 15mg/kg IV q12h ($) R
